passage: Dusk was falling and Karthik and his friend Zubin had no phone between them when Zubin's front wheel slid off the ramp of bricks. Karthik had said yes to the stunt because everyone was watching, and he could feel that yes in his stomach now. Zubin sat holding his wrist, pale and silent. "Stay here," Karthik said, and ran home in one breath. "Papa, Zubin fell off the brick ramp and his wrist is hurt. I joined in too. I should have said no." His father grabbed the car keys. At the clinic Karthik sat beside Zubin until Zubin's mother arrived. Next time, Karthik promised himself, the no would come first.

qa.q: Why could the boys not call for help from where they were?
qa.a: Neither boy had a phone and dusk was falling.

qa.q: What was Karthik feeling as he watched Zubin hold his wrist?
qa.a: Guilty and worried, since he felt the yes in his stomach and ran straight home for help.

qa.q: What could Karthik do next time a risky stunt is proposed?
qa.a: Say no early and suggest a safer trick, and tell an adult if the group keeps pushing.

qa.q: How might Karthik's father feel when Karthik told him?
qa.a: Alarmed for Zubin but glad that Karthik came straight away and told the truth.

grounding: After a friend is hurt on a risky bicycle stunt, a boy admits he should have refused, tells his father and helps his friend.

passage: The ramp was just a plank on two bricks in the parking lot of Shankar's building in Pune. Varun wanted to jump it with no hands. "You try first, Shankar, then I'll beat you." Shankar did it holding on, wobbling. Varun let go of the handlebars in mid-air and hit the concrete shoulder first. His elbow was bleeding and his cheek was scraped. Shankar ran for the watchman, then pressed his own hanky on the elbow while they waited for Varun's mother. That evening he told his parents everything, including that the ramp was his idea. "I knew it was silly before we started," he said. "Next time I'll say it before, not after." His father nodded and walked him over to Varun's flat with a box of laddoos.

qa.q: What was the ramp made of?
qa.a: It was a plank on two bricks.

qa.q: What might Shankar have been feeling when he told his parents the ramp was his idea?
qa.a: He likely felt guilty and ashamed, but he also wanted to be honest so he could start putting things right.

qa.q: What would Shankar change first next time, and why?
qa.a: He would speak up before the stunt starts, because saying it is silly early can stop it before anyone gets hurt.

qa.q: How might Varun's family see Shankar's visit with laddoos?
qa.a: They may see that Shankar is honest and sorry, which can help them trust him even though the stunt hurt Varun.

grounding: Shows a boy who joined a risky bicycle stunt helping his hurt friend, telling his parents the truth and resolving to speak up earlier.

passage:
"Joseph, why is your shirt all muddy? And where's your bike?" Mum asked.
"At Gurpreet's. Mum, he fell. We were racing down the quarry hill with no brakes, feet off the pedals."
"Is he hurt?"
"His wrist. His dad took him to the clinic. The doctor said it's a sprain."
Dad put down the newspaper. "Whose idea was the no-brakes part?"
"Gurpreet's. But I said yes. I even went first." Joseph stared at the floor. "I felt bad before we started. I just didn't say it."
"What will you do now?" Mum asked.
"Carry his school bag till his wrist is better. And next time I'll say I'm out before anyone gets on a bike."
"Then let's phone his mum right now," Dad said, reaching for his phone.

qa.a: They were racing down the quarry hill.

qa.q: What does Joseph staring at the floor suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he felt ashamed and guilty, because he had felt bad before the race and said yes anyway 😔.

qa.q: What else could Joseph have done before the race began?
qa.a: He could have said he was out and suggested racing on a flat road with brakes, treating his uneasy feeling as the signal to stop.

qa.q: How do Mum and Dad seem to take Joseph's honesty?
qa.a: They stay calm and ask what he will do, then help him act by phoning Gurpreet's mum, so they seem to value the truth more than scolding.

grounding: Shows a boy admitting to his parents that he should have refused a risky bike race and planning to help his friend and speak up sooner.
